Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 56, verses 1–12:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Idhā waqaʿati al-wāqiʿah﴾: that is, the Resurrection came to pass, and it is called "the Event" (al-wāqiʿah) because it will certainly occur.

﴿Laysa li-waqʿatihā kādhibah﴾: that is, no soul will deny it, as it was denied in the world.

﴿Khāfiḍah rāfiʿah﴾: that is, it will make manifest the lowering of some people by their entry into the Fire, and the raising of others by their entry into the Garden.

﴿Idhā ruijjati al-arḍu rajjā﴾: that is, it will be shaken with a violent shaking.

﴿Wa-bussati al-jibālu bassā﴾: that is, they will be crumbled to dust.

﴿Fa-kānat habāan munbathā﴾: that is, scattered dust.

﴿Wa-kuntum azwājan thalāthah﴾: that is, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be three categories.

﴿Fa-aṣḥābu al-maymanah﴾: that is, those who are given their records in their right hands.

﴿Mā aṣḥābu al-maymanah﴾: an exaltation of their station, by their entry into the Garden.

﴿Wa-aṣḥābu al-mashʾamah﴾: that is, the left-handed, who are given their records in their left hands.

﴿Mā aṣḥābu al-mashʾamah﴾: a belittling of their station, by their entry into the Fire.

﴿Wa-al-sābiqūn﴾: that is, to goodness, and they are those who went before to faith and obedience at the beginning of the call.

﴿Al-sābiqūn﴾: an exaltation of their station.

﴿Ulāʾika al-muqarrabūn﴾: that is, they are the ones brought near, whom Allah will bring near Himself on the Day of Resurrection when He admits them to the Garden.

﴿Fī jannāti al-naʿīm﴾: in gardens of lasting bliss.

Meaning of the verses:

His saying, may He be exalted, confirming the Resurrection and the recompense, which the polytheists denied and rejected with persistence and obstinacy: ﴿When the Event occurs﴾, that is, when the Resurrection comes to pass; ﴿there will be no denial of its occurrence﴾, that is, no soul will deny it, since all will believe in it; ﴿lowering some and raising others﴾, that is, making manifest their state: that they are people of the Fire, and raising others, making manifest their state: that they are among the people of the Garden. And His saying: ﴿When the earth is shaken with a violent shaking﴾, that is, it is moved with a severe motion; ﴿and the mountains are crumbled to powder﴾, that is, when the mountains are crumbled, that is, broken into fine pieces; ﴿and they become scattered dust﴾, that is, dust dispersed.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you will be﴾, that is, O people, ﴿in categories﴾, that is, three kinds: the companions of the right, the companions of the left, and those brought near. The companions of the right (aṣḥābu al-maymanah), or those given their records in their right hands: ﴿what the companions of the right are﴾, that is, their station is great, and that is by their entry into the Garden of bliss. The companions of the left (aṣḥābu al-mashʾamah), who are the left-handed, that is, those who are given their records in their left hands: ﴿what the companions of the left are﴾, that is, their station is base, and that is by their entry into the Fire. And the foremost (al-sābiqūn) to faith and obedience at the first appearance of the call—"the foremost" is an exaltation of their station and a proclamation of their triumph and honour in the Gardens of bliss, which are gardens of lasting bliss. May Allah make us among them.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Confirmation of the Resurrection and the recompense in the Hereafter.

2- Faith and piety raise, while polytheism and sins lower and debase.

3- The foremost in acts of obedience have the merit of precedence in every time and place.

4- The left-handed are the wretched of this world and the Hereafter, because when others took the right hand, seeking faith and uprightness, they took the left hand, seeking disbelief and wickedness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 56, verses 13–26:

Explanation of the words:

*Thullah min al-awwalin* (a multitude of the earlier ones): i.e., a group of the past nations.

*Wa qalilun min al-akhirin* (and a few of the later ones): i.e., from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ). These are the foremost (al-sabiqun).

*Ala sururin mawdunah* (on woven couches, interlaced): i.e., woven and interlaced with gold and jewels.

*Wildanun mukhalladun* (youths made eternal): i.e., in the form of children, who never age, so that they serve them forever.

*Bi-akwabin wa abarik* (with goblets and ewers): the youthful servants circulate among them with goblets, which are cups without handles, and ewers, which have handles and spouts.

*Wa ka'sin min ma'in* (and a cup from a flowing spring): i.e., a vessel for drinking wine; *ma'in* means flowing water from a river that never ceases.

*La yusadda'un* (they will not be afflicted with headache): i.e., no headache will result to them from drinking it.

*Wa la yunzifun* (nor will they be intoxicated): i.e., their minds will not be taken away. It is said: "The drinker was drained (nazafa) and became drained (anzafa)" when his mind was taken away by intoxication.

*Wa fakihatin mimma yatakhayyarun* (and fruits of their choice): i.e., they choose from them what pleases and delights them, even though all of them are delightful.

*Wa huril 'in* (and maidens with beautiful, wide eyes): i.e., they have women with white, large eyes, intensely black and white in their eyes.

*Ka-amthal al-lu'lu' al-maknun* (like hidden pearls): i.e., those maidens of the Garden, in their beauty and purity, are like well-guarded pearls.

*Laghwan wa la ta'thiman* (no idle talk, nor sin): i.e., they will hear in the Garden no idle talk, meaning obscene speech and whatever is of no good, nor anything that leads to sin.

*Illa qilan salaman salaman* (except the saying "Peace, peace"): i.e., they will hear nothing but greetings of peace from the angels and from one another.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues to describe the state of people when the Resurrection occurs. It mentions that they become three categories: the companions of the right, the companions of the left, and the foremost (al-sabiqun). Here He says of the foremost that they are a *thullah*, a multitude, of the earlier ones, i.e., of the past nations, who embraced Islam and preceded to Islam alongside their prophets; and *qalilun min al-akhirin*, a few of the later ones, i.e., of this community, the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), who preceded others in faith, emigration, and jihad. He then mentions their bliss, saying, and His word is the truth: ﴿Upon couches woven together﴾, i.e., they are upon couches woven and interlaced with gold and jewels, reclining on them facing one another, such that none of them looks at the back of another but at his face. ﴿There will circulate among them﴾, i.e., to serve them, ﴿youths made eternal﴾, boys who do not grow old and do not change, but remain so forever. They circulate among them with *akwab*, the plural of *kub*, which is a cup without a handle, and *abarik*, the plural of *ibriq*, which is a vessel with a handle and a spout; and ﴿a cup from a flowing spring﴾. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 56, verses 27–40:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Wa-ashab al-yamin ma ashab al-yamin"* (And the companions of the right, what are the companions of the right): This begins the mention of the second of the three pairs, after mentioning the foremost (al-sabiqun) and what was prepared for them. This is a mention of the companions of the right and what was prepared for them of enduring bliss.

*"Fi sidr makhdud"* (Among lote-trees without thorns): among lote-trees (sidr), whose fruit is the nabq (jujube), and makhdud means without thorns.

*"Wa talhin mandud"* (And acacia trees with fruit piled from top to bottom): that is, banana trees whose fruit is piled from top to bottom, with no bare trunk.

*"Wa zillin mamdud"* (And extended shade): that is, lasting, since no sun cancels it. Indeed, the shade of a single tree in Paradise is such that a rider could travel beneath it for a hundred years without crossing it.

*"Wama'in maskub"* (And water poured out): that is, poured forth. The one enjoying it does not need to pour it with his own hand; rather it flows without a trench or a pipe.

*"La maqtu'a wa la mamnu'a"* (Neither cut off nor forbidden): that is, not cut off at any time, nor withheld by price.

*"Inna ansha'nahunna insha'a"* (Indeed, We have brought them into being in a special creation): that is, the *hur 'in* (wide-eyed maidens), mentioned earlier in His words *"and maidens with wide, lovely eyes."* Each of them in this world was an old, gray-haired, bleary-eyed, dim-sighted woman, and her Lord brings her into being anew, a virgin, coquettish, passionate, and affectionate toward her husband.

*"Faja'alnahunna abkara"* (And We have made them virgins): the singular is *bikr*, one who has not yet had her virginity taken; she is called *adhra'* (virgin).

*"Uruban"* (Loving, devoted): the singular is *arub*, one who is affectionate toward her husband and good in her devotion to him.

*"Atraban"* (Of equal age): that is, of the same age. The singular is *tirb*, and the plural is *atrab*.

*"Li-ashab al-yamin"* (For the companions of the right): those who are taken to the right on the plains of Resurrection; they are the people of faith in this world and of righteous deeds in it.

*"Thullatun min al-awwalin"* (A multitude from the earlier peoples): that is, from the previous nations.

*"Wa thullatun min al-akhirin"* (And a multitude from the later ones): that is, from the Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ).

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to present the conditions of the Hereafter and to mention what belongs to each of the three categories of people: the foremost, the companions of the right, and the companions of the left. God, the Exalted, says: *"And the companions of the right, what are the companions of the right?"* They are those who, when they stand on the plains of Resurrection, will be taken to the right; they are the people of faith and piety in this world. His words *"what are the companions of the right"* magnify their station and proclaim their honour. Then He explains this with His words: *"Among lote-trees without thorns, and acacia trees with fruit piled from top to bottom, and extended shade, and water poured out, and fruit abundant, neither cut off nor forbidden, and raised couches."* Indeed, in this enduring bliss they will eat of the nabq, which is sweeter than honey and more pleasant than butter; its tree is thornless, having no thorns on it. They will also eat of the talh, that is its fruit, which is the banana, and of flowing water, and of abundant fruit that is not cut off by the seasons of the year, as is the case with the fruit of this world, where some is available in summer and not in winter, for example; nor is it forbidden by a high or low price. And on raised couches, as high as the degrees of rank in which they are.

His words *"Indeed, We have brought them into being in a special creation"* refer to the *hur 'in* mentioned earlier in the verses. Among them are the women of this world: there were black women, dim-sighted women, bleary-eyed women, and old women. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 56, verses 41–56:

Explanation of the words:

"And the companions of the left" (wa-ashab al-shimal): that is, those who are taken by the left side (dhat al-shimal) at the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, and they are the people of polytheism (shirk) and sin in the world.

"In scorching wind" (fi samum): that is, a hot wind that penetrates the pores of the body.

"And boiling water" (wa-hamim): that is, water that is extremely hot.

"And a shade of black smoke" (wa-zill min yahmum): that is, smoke that is intensely black.

"Neither cool nor pleasant" (la barid wa-la karim): that is, not cool like other shades, nor fine-looking in appearance.

"They were before that" (kanu qabla dhalika): that is, in the world.

"Living in luxury" (mutrafin): that is, enjoying comforts, not rising to the legal obligations, and not exerting themselves in obedience to Allah and His Messenger.

"Persisted in the great violation" (yusirrun ala al-hinth al-azim): that is, the great sin, which is polytheism.

"And they used to say: 'When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised again?'" (wa-kanu yaqulun a-idha mitna al-an): that is, they used to deny the final resurrection.

"Gathered to the appointed time of a known day" (lamajmu'un ila miqati yawm ma'lum): that is, to the time of a known day, which is the Day of Resurrection.

"O you who are astray, who deny" (ayyuha al-dallun al-mukadhdhibun): that is, you who are astray from the path of guidance, who deny the resurrection and the recompense.

"From a tree of zaqqum" (min shajar min zaqqum): that is, from the most vile of trees, bitter to the utmost in its repulsiveness and ugliness in taste and color.

"Drinking as thirsty camels drink" (fa-sharibun sharb al-him): that is, drinking as thirsty camels drink, for al-hayman is the thirsty one and al-haymá is the parched female.

"This is their hospitality on the Day of Judgment" (hadha nuzuluhum yawm al-din): that is, this is what has been prepared for them as provision (qira) on the Day of Recompense and Reckoning, which is the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to explain the conditions of the three categories into which humanity divides when it emerges from its graves. It mentioned the condition of the foremost (al-sabiqun) and the condition of the companions of the right (ashab al-yamin), and here it mentions the condition of the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'ama), who are the companions of the left. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left?﴾ a denunciation of their condition and an announcement of the evil of their end and of the punishment they are in. Indeed they are ﴿in scorching wind﴾, that is, a hot wind that penetrates the pores of the body, ﴿and boiling water﴾, which is water extremely hot; this is their drink, ﴿and a shade of black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant﴾. It is dense black smoke, ﴿neither cool﴾ like other shades, ﴿nor pleasant﴾, that is, not fine-looking in its appearance. As for His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Indeed they were before that living in luxury﴾, this is the reason for their recompense with painful punishment: they were in the world enjoying comforts, not praying, not fasting, not striving, and not standing guard, ﴿and they used to persist in the great violation﴾, that is, in great sin, namely polytheism and major sins and abominations.

﴿And they used to say﴾, denying the resurrection and recompense, rejecting the Last Day: ﴿"When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we indeed be raised?"﴾, that is, alive as we were in the world, ﴿"or our forefathers too?"﴾, that they too would be raised in the same way. The interrogation in both places is for disbelief and denial. Here Allah the Exalted commands His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) to answer them with His saying, ﴿Say﴾, that is, say to them: ﴿"Indeed, the former and the latter"﴾, that is, you and your forefathers from the time of Adam, and the later ones among you and your descendants until the end of human life, ﴿"are gathered to the appointed time of a known day"﴾, that is, to a time of a day known to Allah, determined by the day, the hour, and the minute. ﴿Then indeed you, O you who are astray﴾ from the way of guidance, who turn away from the truth and deny the resurrection, ﴿are to enter Hell, abiding therein forever.﴾ Indeed you ﴿will eat from a tree of zaqqum﴾, which is the worst fruit and the most vile of things to eat in bitterness, ﴿and you will fill your bellies with it﴾ because of the severe hunger that will afflict you. ﴿Then you will drink upon it from the boiling water, and you will drink as the thirsty camels drink﴾, that is, boiling water extremely hot, drinking in great quantity as thirsty camels drink, which are afflicted by thirst and by the intense disease of hayam that has struck them.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿This is their hospitality on the Day of Judgment﴾, that is, what we have mentioned of the food and drink of the astray deniers is their hospitality which We will host them with on the Day of Judgment. The original meaning of nuzul is what is prepared for the arriving guest: food, drink, and bedding.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1. The companions of the left include every disbeliever who has existed on the face of the earth, for in the division they are one third of humanity, while in reality they are many times more than the foremost and the companions of the right, because most people do not believe.

2. The denunciation of luxury and comfort in this worldly life, for it leads to abandoning the legal obligations, so its possessor is destroyed, not because his food is abundant or his drink delicious.

3. The affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense with no further addition, through the presentation and description of the condition of people.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 56, verses 57–74:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Nahnu khalaqnakum﴾: That is, We brought you into existence from nothing.

﴿Falawla tusaddiqun﴾: That is, why then do you not believe in the Resurrection? For the One Who is able to originate creation is able to restore it after annihilation and decay.

﴿Afara'aytum ma tumnun﴾: That is, that which you emit as semen through intercourse into the wombs of your women.

﴿A-antum takhluqunahu﴾: That is, do you create it as a human being, or are We the Creators of it as a human being?

﴿Nahnu qaddarna baynakum al-mawt﴾: That is, We have decreed death upon you, written it for you, and appointed for each one of you a specific term that he cannot exceed or come before, under any circumstances.

﴿Wa ma nahnu bi-masbuqin﴾: That is, We are not incapable.

﴿Ala an nubaddila amthalakum﴾: That is, [We are not incapable of changing] what you are in creation and form.

﴿Wa nunshi'akum fima la ta'lamun﴾: That is, and We will bring you into forms you do not know. This is a threat to them of transforming them into the most hideous and ugliest of animals.

﴿Wa laqad 'alimtumu al-nash'at al-ula﴾: That is, you have certainly known how We created you and how it was accomplished and how it came to be.

﴿Afala tadhakkarun﴾: So that you would know that He Who created you the first time is able to recreate you again after your death and annihilation.

﴿Afara'aytum ma tahrathun﴾: That is, from stirring the earth with the plough and casting seed into it.

﴿A-antum tazra'unahu﴾: That is, do you make it grow?

﴿Am nahnu al-zari'un﴾: That is, We are the ones who cause it to grow. It is said: zara'ahu Allah, meaning He caused it to grow.

﴿Law nashau laja'alnahu hutaman﴾: That is, if We willed, We would make the crop into dry, withered debris after it had become an ear of grain and nearly ripened for harvest, so that you would be deprived of it.

﴿Fazaltum tafakkahun﴾: That is, you would marvel in your gatherings at the calamity that struck your crop.

﴿Inna lamughramun﴾: That is, saying, "We are indeed burdened [with debt]," meaning: what we spent on its ploughing and tending is a punishment for us.

﴿Bal nahnu mahrumun﴾: That is, we are not punished by it, but rather we are deprived of our crop, and what we expended on it yields us no portion or good fortune, meaning we are neither favoured nor blessed.

﴿Afara'aytum al-ma' alladhi tashrabun﴾: That is, tell us about the water that you drink, on which your life depends.

﴿A-antum anzaltumuhu min al-muzn﴾: That is, from the clouds in the sky down to the earth.

﴿Am nahnu al-munzilun﴾: That is, down to the earth.

﴿Law nashau laja'alnahu ujaja﴾: That is, salty and bitter, impossible to drink.

﴿Falawla tashkurun﴾: That is, why do you not give thanks, meaning thanks to God through faith and obedience.

﴿Afara'aytum al-nar allati tûrun﴾: That is, tell us about the fire that you kindle from the tree.

﴿A-antum ansha'tum shajaratha﴾: That is, did you create its tree, such as the markh, the 'afar and the kalakh?

﴿Am nahnu al-munshi'un﴾: That is, We are the ones who produce those trees.

﴿Nahnu ja'alnaha tadhkira﴾: That is, We made that fire a reminder, reminding of the fire of Hell.

﴿Wa mata'an lil-muqwin﴾: That is, a provision for travellers, by which they sustain themselves on their journeys.

﴿Fasabbih bi-smi rabbika al-'azim﴾: That is, exalt the name of your Lord above what is not fitting for it, such as mentioning it without respect and reverence. Or the word "ism" is superfluous and the meaning is: exalt your Lord above having partners; and from this is your saying, "Subhana rabbiya al-'azim" (Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty).

Meaning of the verses:

The context here is the affirmation of the belief in the Resurrection and recompense, which the polytheists denied, by mentioning the rational proofs that produce knowledge and certainty regarding the matter sought to be established. The Exalted said, ﴿Nahnu khalaqnakum﴾, while you yourselves acknowledge this, for when we ask you who created you, you say, "God."

Thus, ﴿Falawla tusaddiqun﴾: that is, why do you not believe in the resurrection and the second life, since the One Who is able to create at first is able to restore? These are evidences of Our power; consider them first. ﴿Afara'aytum ma tumnun﴾: that is, tell us about what you emit, which you pour into the wombs of your women through intercourse. ﴿A-antum takhluqunahu﴾ as a child. ﴿Am nahnu al-khaliqun﴾. The answer is: We are the Creators. Thus, the One Who creates you through this emission and formation in the wombs is able to create you by another means. Second, ﴿Nahnu qaddarna baynakum al-mawt﴾ and We have decreed it upon you, so none of you can prevent Us from causing him to die or from doing so at the appointed time, such that if he asked for it to be advanced or delayed, he would not be able to do so. Is not the One Who creates you and causes you to die able to resurrect you? Indeed. Third, ﴿Wa ma nahnu bi-masbuqin ala an nubaddila amthalakum wa nunshi'akum fi ma la ta'lamun﴾: by creating you in forms and shapes other than what you are, creating you as a hideous and ugly creature, like apes and swine. We are not incapable of that; will We then be incapable of resurrecting you after your death, alive, to call you to account and recompense you? ﴿Wa laqad 'alimtumu al-nash'at al-ula﴾: how it was accomplished for you, through what you do not deny.

Thus, ﴿Falawla tadhakkarun﴾: so that you would know that He Who created you the first time is able to create you again, given the knowledge that re-creation is no harder than origination from nothing, not from existence. Fourth, ﴿Afara'aytum ma tahrathun﴾ from stirring the earth and casting seed into it; tell us, do you make it grow? ﴿Am nahnu al-zari'un﴾ of it, that is, the ones who cause it to grow? The answer is well known: it is We who cause it to grow, not you. Thus, the One Who causes the crop to grow is able to cause you to grow in your graves in the manner of the growth of the crop, and the coccyx is the seed from which you grow. Fifth, that crop which We caused to grow: if We willed, We would make it, after its freshness and nearness to harvest, into dry debris from which you derive no benefit whatsoever. Then you would marvel, astonished at your deprivation of your crop, saying, ﴿Inna lamughramun﴾, that is, what we spent on its ploughing and tending is a punishment upon us. Then you turn away from that saying to another saying, which is your saying, ﴿Bal nahnu mahrumun﴾: we have no portion or good fortune in it, that is, we are neither favoured nor blessed. Thus, the One Who causes the crop to grow is able to cause you to grow in your graves in the manner of the growth of the crop, and the coccyx is the seed from which you grow. Fifth, that crop which We caused to grow: if We willed, We would make it, after its freshness and nearness to harvest, into dry debris from which you derive no benefit whatsoever. Then you would marvel, astonished at your deprivation of your crop, saying, ﴿Inna lamughramun﴾, that is, what we spent on its ploughing and tending is a punishment upon us. So why do you not give thanks for this kindness from Us to you, by believing in Us and obeying Us? Seventh, the fire that you kindle and ignite, tell me: ﴿A-antum ansha'tum shajaratha am nahnu al-munshi'un﴾? The answer: We, not you. For the Resurrection and the Hereafter are the goal of this worldly life: people act so that they may be called to account and recompensed. ﴿Wa laqad 'alimtumu al-nash'at al-ula﴾: That is, you have certainly known how We created you and how it was accomplished and how it came to be.

﴿Afala tadhakkarun﴾: So that you would know that He Who created you the first time is able to recreate you again after your death and annihilation.

﴿Afara'aytum ma tahrathun﴾: That is, from stirring the earth with the plough and casting seed into it.

﴿A-antum tazra'unahu﴾: That is, do you make it grow?

﴿Am nahnu al-zari'un﴾: That is, We are the ones who cause it to grow. It is said: zara'ahu Allah, meaning He caused it to grow.

﴿Law nashau laja'alnahu hutaman﴾: That is, if We willed, We would make the crop into dry, withered debris after it had become an ear of grain and nearly ripened for harvest, so that you would be deprived of it.

﴿Fazaltum tafakkahun﴾: That is, you would marvel in your gatherings at the calamity that struck your crop.

﴿Inna lamughramun﴾: That is, saying, "We are indeed burdened [with debt]," meaning: what we spent on its ploughing and tending is a punishment for us.

﴿Bal nahnu mahrumun﴾: That is, we are not punished by it, but rather we are deprived of our crop, and what we expended on it yields us no portion or good fortune, meaning we are neither favoured nor blessed.

﴿Afara'aytum al-ma' alladhi tashrabun﴾: That is, tell us about the water that you drink, on which your life depends.

﴿A-antum anzaltumuhu min al-muzn﴾: That is, from the clouds in the sky down to the earth.

﴿Am nahnu al-munzilun﴾: That is, down to the earth.

﴿Law nashau laja'alnahu ujaja﴾: That is, salty and bitter, impossible to drink.

﴿Falawla tashkurun﴾: That is, why do you not give thanks, meaning thanks to God through faith and obedience.

﴿Afara'aytum al-nar allati tûrun﴾: That is, tell us about the fire that you kindle from the tree.

﴿A-antum ansha'tum shajaratha﴾: That is, did you create its tree, such as the markh, the 'afar and the kalakh?

﴿Am nahnu al-munshi'un﴾: That is, We are the ones who produce those trees.

﴿Nahnu ja'alnaha tadhkira﴾: That is, We made that fire a reminder, reminding of the fire of Hell.

﴿Wa mata'an lil-muqwin﴾: That is, a provision for travellers, by which they sustain themselves on their journeys.

﴿Fasabbih bi-smi rabbika al-'azim﴾: That is, exalt the name of your Lord above what is not fitting for it, such as mentioning it without respect and reverence. Or the word "ism" is superfluous and the meaning is: exalt your Lord above having partners; and from this is your saying, "Subhana rabbiya al-'azim" (Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty).

Meaning of the verses:

The context here is the affirmation of the belief in the Resurrection and recompense, which the polytheists denied, by mentioning the rational proofs that produce knowledge and certainty regarding the matter sought to be established. The Exalted said, ﴿Nahnu khalaqnakum﴾, while you yourselves acknowledge this, for when we ask you who created you, you say, "God."

Thus, ﴿Falawla tusaddiqun﴾: that is, why do you not believe in the resurrection and the second life, since the One Who is able to create at first is able to restore? These are evidences of Our power; consider them first. ﴿Afara'aytum ma tumnun﴾: that is, tell us about what you emit, which you pour into the wombs of your women through intercourse. ﴿A-antum takhluqunahu﴾ as a child. ﴿Am nahnu al-khaliqun﴾. The answer is: We are the Creators. Thus, the One Who creates you through this emission and formation in the wombs is able to create you by another means. Second, ﴿Nahnu qaddarna baynakum al-mawt﴾ and We have decreed it upon you, so none of you can prevent Us from causing him to die or from doing so at the appointed time, such that if he asked for it to be advanced or delayed, he would not be able to do so. Is not the One Who creates you and causes you to die able to resurrect you? Indeed. Third, ﴿Wa ma nahnu bi-masbuqin ala an nubaddila amthalakum wa nunshi'akum fi ma la ta'lamun﴾: by creating you in forms and shapes other than what you are, creating you as a hideous and ugly creature, like apes and swine. We are not incapable of that; will We then be incapable of resurrecting you after your death, alive, to call you to account and recompense you? ﴿Wa laqad 'alimtumu al-nash'at al-ula﴾: how it was accomplished for you, through what you do not deny.

Thus, ﴿Falawla tadhakkarun﴾: so that you would know that He Who created you the first time is able to create you again, given the knowledge that re-creation is no harder than origination from nothing, not from existence. Fourth, ﴿Afara'aytum ma tahrathun﴾ from stirring the earth and casting seed into it; tell us, do you make it grow? ﴿Am nahnu al-zari'un﴾ of it, that is, the ones who cause it to grow? The answer is well known: it is We who cause it to grow, not you. Thus, the One Who causes the crop to grow is able to cause you to grow in your graves in the manner of the growth of the crop, and the coccyx is the seed from which you grow. Fifth, that crop which We caused to grow: if We willed, We would make it, after its freshness and nearness to harvest, into dry debris from which you derive no benefit whatsoever. Then you would marvel, astonished at your deprivation of your crop, saying, ﴿Inna lamughramun﴾, that is, what we spent on its ploughing and tending is a punishment upon us. Then you turn away from that saying to another saying, which is your saying, ﴿Bal nahnu mahrumun﴾: we have no portion or good fortune in it, that is, we are neither favoured nor blessed. The growth of the crop and then your deprivation of it, after your hope of benefiting from it, is a manifestation of the manifestations of God's power, knowledge, wisdom and governance, all of which indicate His power to resurrect you to call you to account and recompense you for your deeds in this worldly life. Sixth, the water that you drink, on which your life depends: tell me, ﴿A-antum anzaltumuhu﴾ from the clouds, ﴿Am nahnu al-munzilun﴾? The answer: We are the ones who send it down, not you. This is first; second, if We willed, We would make the water salty and bitter, from which you would derive no benefit whatsoever, and We are indeed able to do so. So why do you not give thanks for this kindness from Us to you, by believing in Us and obeying Us? Seventh, the fire that you kindle and ignite, tell me: ﴿A-antum ansha'tum shajaratha am nahnu al-munshi'un﴾? The answer: We, not you. So He Who brings fire into being in the tree is able to raise you alive from your graves to call you to account for your conduct and recompense you for it.

As for His saying, ﴿Nahnu ja'alnaha﴾, that is, the fire, ﴿tadhkiratan﴾ for you, reminding you of the fire of the Hereafter. So He Who brought this fire into being is able to bring about another fire, if you would only remember. We have also made it ﴿mata'an﴾, that is, a provision for the travellers (al-muqwin), by which they sustain themselves on their journey until they return to their homes. Thus, the One Who creates, brings into being and governs the interests of His servants is able to bring about another life in which He will recompense the good-doers for their good and the evildoers for their evil, since wisdom requires this and commands it.

As for His saying, ﴿Fasabbih bi-smi rabbika al-'azim﴾, after establishing the proof against those who deny the Resurrection by rational proofs, the Exalted commanded His Messenger to glorify his Lord, that is, to exalt Him above play and purposelessness, which would be implied by the creation of this worldly life on this precise order and then its annihilation with nothing beyond it. For the Resurrection and the Hereafter are the goal of this worldly life: people act so that they may be called to account and recompensed. Therefore there must be a life more complete and perfect than this life, in which recompense is completed. The Exalted has explained and detailed it in His books and through the tongues of His messengers, and has set forth examples of it. None denies it except a foolish, doomed person.

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Affirmation of the belief in the Resurrection and recompense.

2- Establishing the many proofs and demonstrations of the validity and possibility of the Resurrection by reason.

3- Explanation of the favours of the Exalted upon His servants in their food and drink.

4- The obligation to thank God for His bounty and blessings.

5- In the fire that you kindle there is a lesson and admonition for the God-fearing.

6- The obligation to glorify God and exalt Him above what is unbefitting to His majesty and perfection, such as futility and partners.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 56, verses 75–82:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Fa-la uqsimu﴾: meaning, "fa-uqsimu" (so I swear). The "la" is not a negation but is added to strengthen the speech and emphasize the oath.

Bi-mawaqi' al-nujum (by the positions of the stars): meaning, by their setting-places (sawaqit) when they set, and also by their stations (manazil) and their risings (matali') likewise.

Wa-innahu (and indeed it): meaning, the oath by them.

Law ta'lamuna 'azim (if you knew, it is a great [oath]): meaning, if you were people of knowledge, you would know the greatness of the oath.

Innahu (indeed it): meaning, what is recited to you is a noble Qur'an, and it is what the polytheists denied.

Fi kitabin maknun (in a hidden Book): meaning, protected; this is the mushaf.

La yamassuhu illa al-mutahharun (none touches it except the purified): meaning, from among the angels and the prophets and every pure person who is not in a state of major or minor ritual impurity (hadath).

Tanzilun min rabbi al-'alamin (a revelation from the Lord of the worlds): meaning, sent down from the Lord of the worlds, who is Allah, majestic is His majesty.

Afa-hadha al-hadith (is it this discourse?): meaning, the Qur'an.

Antum mudhinun (that you are disdainful/compromising): meaning, you soften speech toward those who deny it, in collusion with them in denying it and disbelieving.

Wa taj'aluna rizqakum (and you make your provision): meaning, you make your thanks to God for your provision

Annakum tukadhdhibun (that you deny): meaning, your denial of God's giving of rain, and you say, "We were given rain by such-and-such a star's setting (nawʾ)."

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars﴾: meaning, I swear by the positions of the stars, which are their risings and their settings. ﴿And indeed it is a great oath, if you knew﴾: meaning, if you were people of knowledge. Because the stars, their stations, their risings, their setting-places, and the places where they set contain great matters in their creation and in God's governance of them, indeed it is an oath by a great thing.

The sworn matter is His words, ﴿indeed it is a noble Qur'an﴾, not as the falsifiers say: poetry, sorcery, lies, or fabrication. ﴿In a Book well-guarded﴾: meaning, protected; whether it is in the Preserved Tablet or in our mushafs. ﴿None touches it but the purified﴾: therefore none should touch it except those purified from minor and major ritual impurities. ﴿A revelation from the Lord of the worlds﴾: meaning, sent down from Him, glorified and exalted; therefore it is obligatory to sanctify and honor it, and none should touch it except one purified from shirk, disbelief, and all impurities.

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Is it this discourse that you are disdainful of?﴾: meaning, the Qur'an. ﴿That you soften speech toward those who deny it, colluding with them in denial and disbelief﴾; ﴿and you make your provision﴾: meaning, you make the thanks to God for His provision to you ﴿that you deny﴾: meaning, your denial of God's giving you rain, and you say, "We were given rain by such-and-such a star, and such-and-such a star."

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification that God swears by whatever He wills of His creation, and that a servant should swear only by his Lord, exalted is He.

2- Affirmation of divine revelation and establishment of Muhammad's prophethood, and that the noble Qur'an was sent down from God, exalted is He.

3- The obligation to safeguard the noble Qur'an, and the prohibition of touching it without ritual purity.

4- The prohibition of mudahana (compromise) in the religion of God, which is to concede some of the religion in order to preserve some of one's worldly affairs; and mudara (diplomatic tact) is permissible, which is to concede some of one's worldly affairs in order to preserve some of one's religion.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 56, verses 83–96:

Explanation of the words:

Falawla (فلولا): meaning "why not" (fahallā), and it is used to urge and incite action.

Idha balaghat al-halqum (إذا بلغت الحلقوم): meaning the passage of food, and that is the time of death throes (nazʿ).

Wa-antum tanzurun (وأنتم تنظرون): meaning, and you, O nursing attendants and visitors, are looking at him.

Wa-nahnu aqrabu ilayhi minkum (ونحن أقرب إليه منكم): meaning, and Our messengers, the Angel of Death and his assistants, are closer to the dying person than you are.

Wa-lakin la tubsirun (ولكن لا تبصرون): meaning, the angels.

Falawla in kuntum ghayra madinin (فلولا إن كنتم غير مدينين): meaning, why not, if you are not owed (not held to account) after death.

Tarji'unaha in kuntum sadiqin (ترجعونها إن كنتم صادقين): meaning, you return the soul to the body after its departure from it, if you are truthful in your claim that you will not be resurrected or held to account.

Fa-amma in kana (فأما إن كان): meaning, the dying person.

Min al-muqarrabin (من المقربين): meaning, from the foremost, who are the first of the three categories mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Fa-rawhun wa-rayhan (فروح وريحان): meaning, rest and fragrance, that is, good provision and gardens of bliss.

Wa-amma in kana min ashab al-yamin (وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين): meaning, from the second category, so, "Peace be upon you, O companion of the right hand, from among the companions of the right hand." That is, your brethren greet you, for they are in the gardens of bliss.

Fa-nuzulun min hamim (فنزل من حميم): meaning, for him is a lodging of boiling water of intense heat.

Wa-tasliyatu jahim (وتصلية جحيم): meaning, burning in it.

Inna hadha lahuwa haqqu al-yaqin (إن هذا لهو حق اليقين): meaning, what We have related to you in this surah is indeed the certain truth.

Fa-sabbih bi-smi rabbika al-azim (فسبح باسم ربك العظيم): meaning, glorify and sanctify the name of your Lord, the Mighty.

Meaning of the verses:

After affirming the Prophethood of Muhammad and that the Qur'an is the speech of God and its revelation, the noble context returns to affirming the Resurrection and the recompense. God the Exalted says: ﴿Why then, when the soul reaches the throat﴾, that is, the soul, ﴿the throat﴾, which is the passage of food, ﴿and you at that time﴾ ﴿are looking on﴾ at your sick person, who is suffering the agonies of death. ﴿And We are nearer to him than you﴾, that is, Our messengers are nearer to him than you, ﴿but you do not see﴾, for you have no power to see the angels unless they take the form of a human being. His saying ﴿Why then, if you are not under judgment﴾ means, not held accountable after death and not recompensed for your deeds, ﴿would you not return the soul﴾ after it has reached the throat, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that you are not owed to God for your deeds, that is, that He will not call you to account for them or recompense you for them.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿As for if he was﴾, that is, the dying person, ﴿among those brought near﴾, who are the foremost, ﴿then there is rest and bounty﴾, that is, for him is complete rest from the hardship of worldly toil and its burdens, and bounty, which is good provision, and a Garden of Delight. As for if he was among the companions of the right hand, who will be taken by the right side on the plains of Resurrection, then: ﴿Peace be upon you, O companion of the right hand﴾, from your brethren, the companions of the right hand, who have preceded you to the Abode of Peace.

As for if the dying person was among those who denied God and His Messenger, who denied the Last Resurrection and who strayed from guidance and the religion of truth, then ﴿for him is a lodging of boiling water﴾, that is, a hospitality of hot water; this is his hospitality, ﴿and burning in Hellfire﴾, that is, being scorched in the Hellfire.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty﴾, that is, what We have told you about the three categories of the dying, and what is theirs, and what they will attain, is the true certainty.

His saying ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ commands His Messenger to glorify the name of his Mighty Lord. It is authentically reported that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said to his companions, "Place it in your bowing (rukuʿ)." Tasbih means sanctifying and declaring God free of anything unbecoming to His majesty and perfection.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of Resurrection and recompense.

2. Demonstration of the helplessness of all people before the power of God the Exalted.

3. That the human inability to return the soul of the dying so that he may live on, even for an hour, is evidence that there is no god but God.

4. Explanation of the virtue of the foremost over the companions of the right hand.

5. The Noble Qur'an: all its rulings are just and all its reports are true.

6. The legitimacy of the servant saying "Subhan Allah wa-bihamdih" and "Subhan Allah al-Azim", both of which are among the good words, and likewise "Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim" during bowing.

6. The legitimacy of the servant saying "Subhan Allah wa-bihamdih" and "Subhan Allah al-Azim", both of which are among the good words, and likewise "Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim" during bowing.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 56, verses 83–96:

Explanation of the words:

Falawla (فلولا): meaning "why not" (fahallā), and it is used to urge and incite action.

Idha balaghat al-halqum (إذا بلغت الحلقوم): meaning the passage of food, and that is the time of death throes (nazʿ).

Wa-antum tanzurun (وأنتم تنظرون): meaning, and you, O nursing attendants and visitors, are looking at him.

Wa-nahnu aqrabu ilayhi minkum (ونحن أقرب إليه منكم): meaning, and Our messengers, the Angel of Death and his assistants, are closer to the dying person than you are.

Wa-lakin la tubsirun (ولكن لا تبصرون): meaning, the angels.

Falawla in kuntum ghayra madinin (فلولا إن كنتم غير مدينين): meaning, why not, if you are not owed (not held to account) after death.

Tarji'unaha in kuntum sadiqin (ترجعونها إن كنتم صادقين): meaning, you return the soul to the body after its departure from it, if you are truthful in your claim that you will not be resurrected or held to account.

Fa-amma in kana (فأما إن كان): meaning, the dying person.

Min al-muqarrabin (من المقربين): meaning, from the foremost, who are the first of the three categories mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

Fa-rawhun wa-rayhan (فروح وريحان): meaning, rest and fragrance, that is, good provision and gardens of bliss.

Wa-amma in kana min ashab al-yamin (وأما إن كان من أصحاب اليمين): meaning, from the second category, so, "Peace be upon you, O companion of the right hand, from among the companions of the right hand." That is, your brethren greet you, for they are in the gardens of bliss.

Fa-nuzulun min hamim (فنزل من حميم): meaning, for him is a lodging of boiling water of intense heat.

Wa-tasliyatu jahim (وتصلية جحيم): meaning, burning in it.

Inna hadha lahuwa haqqu al-yaqin (إن هذا لهو حق اليقين): meaning, what We have related to you in this surah is indeed the certain truth.

Fa-sabbih bi-smi rabbika al-azim (فسبح باسم ربك العظيم): meaning, glorify and sanctify the name of your Lord, the Mighty.

Meaning of the verses:

After affirming the Prophethood of Muhammad and that the Qur'an is the speech of God and its revelation, the noble context returns to affirming the Resurrection and the recompense. God the Exalted says: ﴿Why then, when the soul reaches the throat﴾, that is, the soul, ﴿the throat﴾, which is the passage of food, ﴿and you at that time﴾ ﴿are looking on﴾ at your sick person, who is suffering the agonies of death. ﴿And We are nearer to him than you﴾, that is, Our messengers are nearer to him than you, ﴿but you do not see﴾, for you have no power to see the angels unless they take the form of a human being. His saying ﴿Why then, if you are not under judgment﴾ means, not held accountable after death and not recompensed for your deeds, ﴿would you not return the soul﴾ after it has reached the throat, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that you are not owed to God for your deeds, that is, that He will not call you to account for them or recompense you for them.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿As for if he was﴾, that is, the dying person, ﴿among those brought near﴾, who are the foremost, ﴿then there is rest and bounty﴾, that is, for him is complete rest from the hardship of worldly toil and its burdens, and bounty, which is good provision, and a Garden of Delight. As for if he was among the companions of the right hand, who will be taken by the right side on the plains of Resurrection, then: ﴿Peace be upon you, O companion of the right hand﴾, from your brethren, the companions of the right hand, who have preceded you to the Abode of Peace.

As for if the dying person was among those who denied God and His Messenger, who denied the Last Resurrection and who strayed from guidance and the religion of truth, then ﴿for him is a lodging of boiling water﴾, that is, a hospitality of hot water; this is his hospitality, ﴿and burning in Hellfire﴾, that is, being scorched in the Hellfire.

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, this is the true certainty﴾, that is, what We have told you about the three categories of the dying, and what is theirs, and what they will attain, is the true certainty.

His saying ﴿So glorify the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ commands His Messenger to glorify the name of his Mighty Lord. It is authentically reported that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ said to his companions, "Place it in your bowing (rukuʿ)." Tasbih means sanctifying and declaring God free of anything unbecoming to His majesty and perfection.

Guidance from the verses:

1. Affirmation of the doctrine of Resurrection and recompense.

2. Demonstration of the helplessness of all people before the power of God the Exalted.

3. That the human inability to return the soul of the dying so that he may live on, even for an hour, is evidence that there is no god but God.

4. Explanation of the virtue of the foremost over the companions of the right hand.

5. The Noble Qur'an: all its rulings are just and all its reports are true.

6. The legitimacy of the servant saying "Subhan Allah wa-bihamdih" and "Subhan Allah al-Azim", both of which are among the good words, and likewise "Subhana Rabbiya al-Azim" during bowing.
